passage: On Salma's first day at the new school, the plan was clear in the head: sit next to the girl with the green hair band, then say "Hi, I'm Salma. Can I sit here?" All through the maths class, Salma rehearsed it, word by word. By break time, the sentence had become so big that it felt impossible. Salma ate lunch slowly at the end of a bench. Nobody came. Then Joseph, from the next row, sat down two seats away and said, "Are you new? I remember my first day." Salma's shoulders came down. "Yes," said Salma. "I kept meaning to say hi."

qa.q: What was Salma's plan for the first day?
qa.a: To sit next to the girl with the green hair band and say "Hi, I'm Salma. Can I sit here?"

qa.q: Why did the rehearsed sentence start to feel impossible to Salma?
qa.a: Salma kept rehearsing so long that the sentence felt bigger and scarier, showing a fear of being rejected.

qa.q: What could Salma try next time to avoid waiting so long?
qa.a: Say the simple hello early, before the rehearsal grows, since most people welcome a first hello.

qa.q: What might Joseph have wanted when sitting down two seats away and saying "Are you new?"
qa.a: To be kind and welcoming, remembering what a first day is like, and to start a conversation without pushing.

grounding: A child rehearses whom to approach at a new school and waits too long; someone else says hello first.

passage: I'm Vinita, and I sit two rows behind Kiran, who joined our class on Monday. This is what I saw. Kiran opened the lunchbox and closed it again. Kiran looked at our table three times and turned away three times. During the games period, Kiran stood near the wall with the ball in both hands, watching us, and mouthing something quietly, as if practising. I don't know what was going on inside. When I finally said, "Do you want to play with us?" Kiran said, "Yes!" so quickly that I was surprised. Now I say hello to anyone new before I overthink it, in case they are waiting too.

qa.q: What did Kiran do three times near the lunch table?
qa.a: Looked at the table and turned away.

qa.q: What might Kiran have been feeling near the wall, holding the ball?
qa.a: Nervous and wanting to join, though Vinita cannot know for sure what was going on inside.

qa.q: What helped when Vinita spoke up?
qa.a: Vinita offered a simple invitation to play, and Kiran answered yes at once.

qa.q: How might Vinita have felt when Kiran said "Yes!" so quickly?
qa.a: Surprised, as Vinita says, and probably glad, since Vinita now says hello to anyone new before overthinking it.

grounding: A child hesitates at a new school, and an observer sees that the first hello is welcomed.

passage:
Class 5 teacher's note, second week.
Suraj joined us from Nagpur last Monday. Every break, I've seen him stand by the water cooler, looking at the same group of children, especially Sunaina, who sits beside him. Twice he took a step toward them and stopped. His lips moved, as if he were rehearsing. He ate his tiffin alone.
Today I asked him quietly if he'd like to help Sunaina hand out the art sheets. He nodded. While they walked around the room, I heard him say, "Hi. Do you like drawing?" Sunaina said, "Yes! Do you?" and they talked about comics for the rest of the period.
At break he sat with her group. I'll keep giving him small reasons to talk to others this week.

qa.q: Where did Suraj join from?
qa.a: From Nagpur.

qa.q: What was Suraj feeling as he stood by the water cooler?
qa.a: He seemed nervous and afraid of being rejected, rehearsing and stopping himself from approaching.

qa.q: What did the teacher do next that helped?
qa.a: They gave Suraj a small task with Sunaina, which made saying hello easy and led to a real conversation.

qa.q: How did Sunaina respond to Suraj's hello?
qa.a: She welcomed it happily, asking if he liked drawing too.

grounding: Shows a child at a new school rehearsing whom to approach and waiting too long, and how a first hello is welcomed.

passage:
Wednesday
Third day at the new school. I've been planning to talk to Hafsa, the girl with the space pencil box. Monday I planned it all day. "Hi, I like your pencil box." But I didn't say it. Tuesday I got as far as standing next to her at the tap, and then just washed my hands.
Today I kept thinking, what if she ignores me? What if she laughs? What if her friends look at me funny?
At lunch I was so tired of thinking about it that I just said it. "Hi. I like your pencil box." She smiled SO big. "Thanks! It's got glow-in-the-dark planets." Then she said, "Want to sit with us?"
I wasted two days being scared of something that took two seconds.
Ganga

qa.q: What was on Hafsa's pencil box?
qa.a: Glow-in-the-dark planets.

qa.q: What was Ganga worried about before saying hello?
qa.a: Ganga was afraid of being ignored or laughed at, or of her friends looking funny.

qa.q: What would you tell Ganga for the next new school?
qa.a: Say the first hello early, because most people welcome it, and the waiting is harder than the hello.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel when Ganga said hello?
qa.a: She seemed happy, smiling big and inviting Ganga to sit with them.

grounding: Shows a child at a new school rehearsing a hello and waiting too long, then finding the first hello is welcomed.

passage: Afreen's family had moved to the small town of Nabha only a week before. At the school hand pump, she watched a boy named Francis filling his bottle. She'd practised it in her head a dozen times. "Hi, I'm new." But every time she got close, he finished and left. Today she stood behind him again, heart thumping, rehearsing. He finished. He turned. He was leaving. Afreen blurted, "Hi, I'm new. From Ludhiana." Francis stopped. "Oh! Hi! I'm Francis. Do you play kho-kho? We need one more after school." Afreen nodded so fast her plait swung. After school she played kho-kho until her mother came, and on the way home she thought: why did I wait a whole week?

qa.q: Where had Afreen's family moved from?
qa.a: From Ludhiana.

qa.q: How did Afreen feel as she stood behind Francis at the pump?
qa.a: She felt nervous and afraid, her heart thumping, rehearsing what to say.

qa.q: What did Afreen learn by finally saying hello?
qa.a: That the first hello is usually welcomed, since Francis happily invited her to play kho-kho.

qa.q: How did Francis respond to Afreen's hello?
qa.a: He was friendly and welcoming, inviting her to join the game.

grounding: Shows a child in a new town rehearsing whom to approach and waiting too long, then finding her first hello welcomed.

passage: On her third day at the school in Porto, Beatriz stood by the fence at break with her apple, rehearsing. Maybe the girl with the blue plaits. Lucia, the teacher had called her. "Hi, I'm Beatriz, can I play?" No, too babyish. "Hi, what are you playing?" Better. She took a step, then stopped as Lucia laughed with the others. What if they looked at each other? The bell rang. Break was over. That evening she practised the line in the mirror twice. Next day at break she walked straight up before she could think. "Hi, what are you playing?" Lucia blinked. "Elastics. Hold one end, then it's your turn." Just like that. Beatriz wondered why she had waited a whole day.

qa.q: What were the girls playing?
qa.a: They were playing elastics.

qa.q: What was Beatriz worried about when she stopped halfway?
qa.a: She was afraid the girls would look at each other and reject her, so she stayed nervous and waited.

qa.q: What helped Beatriz finally say hello?
qa.a: Walking straight up before she could overthink, with one simple line she had practised.

qa.q: How did Lucia react to the hello?
qa.a: She was welcoming right away, handing Beatriz one end of the elastic and a turn.

grounding: Shows a new child rehearsing whom to approach and waiting too long, then finding her first hello welcomed.
